principles: Conventions before edits: lock a glossary + style guide first, then apply mechanically
Behavior-sensitive code is not prose: isolate it and require tests, never silently retranslate
Preserve the deliverable's verifiable invariants (762<->762, zero Chinese, identifiers, T/M consistency)
drivers: Open-source readiness needs consistent, idiomatic English
An implementer must not mistranslate regex behavior into a runtime change
T/M divergence already produced finding F-005 in B-8448

options.name: Verified-script glossary sweep + manual command-desc shortening + dedicated behavior-sensitive subsection
pros: Count-verified replacements are auditable and safe
Behavior-sensitive rows are clearly quarantined and test-gated
Invariant re-checks are cheap after every pass
cons: Several passes; command-desc shortening needs manual judgement

options.name: Free-form manual re-edit of the whole manifest
cons: Risk of breaking the invariant or T/M consistency

chosen: Verified-script glossary sweep + manual command-desc shortening + dedicated behavior-sensitive subsection
rationale: The count-verified replacement-script approach already worked for the 19 reviewer fixes; reusing it keeps the 762-row sweep safe and auditable, while a dedicated behavior-sensitive subsection plus a reviewStatus marker quarantines the regex rows so they get test updates instead of being silently retranslated. 'real-machine tests' is kept because realMachineTests is a 37-reference code identifier.

preMortem.scenario: A glossary substitution changes a row with a different meaning
preMortem.trigger: Same Chinese/English substring used in two senses (e.g. 执行命令 input vs record)
preMortem.consequence: A wrong translation enters the authoritative manifest
preMortem.mitigation: Use exact-count replacements with expected counts; disambiguate by row ID/surface; review the diff before commit

preMortem.scenario: Editing rows breaks the 762<->762 invariant or introduces Chinese into proposedEnglish
preMortem.trigger: Accidental row add/remove or a bad substitution
preMortem.mitigation: The script re-checks 762 rows + zero Chinese after every pass and aborts on mismatch

preMortem.scenario: Behavior-sensitive regex rows are treated as prose, so a later implementer changes runtime matching
preMortem.trigger: Rows not clearly marked as behavior-sensitive
preMortem.consequence: Silent behavior change when the source is eventually translated
preMortem.mitigation: Enumerate all regex/.test/.match-over-Chinese rows, mark reviewStatus + list them in a dedicated subsection that requires test updates
